newsitem.title: ITALY: BASKETBALL-ITALY TO FACE YUGOSLAVIA IN EUROPEAN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-ITALY TO FACE YUGOSLAVIA IN EUROPEAN FINAL.

text.p: Italy and Yugoslavia will meet in Sunday's European basketball championship final after beating Russia and Greece in their respective semi-finals on Saturday.
Yugoslavia, the holders, were always in control in their 88-80 win over Greece but the Italians were forced to come from behind in their frantic 67-65 win over Russia.
Italy beat the Yugoslavs 74-69 in a group match earlier in the competition, and are yet to lose a match in the tournament but will nervetheless start the game as underdogs.
The Italians looked to be on their way out of the competition after a poor start which left them 28-18 down.
Carlton Myers, tightly guarded by Russia's Sergei Babkov, was slow to find his form.
But it was Myers who turned the game round, and with the Russians giving up several vital possesions in the closing minutes, the Italians were able to hang on.
Earlier, Yugoslavia had played their best game of the tournament to deal with the previously unbeaten Greek side.
Zeljko Obradovic's team went in at the break only four points up, but quickly took control and surged to a 65-50 lead.
The Greeks closed to 74-68, and with five opponents in foul trouble looked likely to give the reigning champions a close run.
But poor shot selection cost the Greeks the chance to draw closer and the Yugoslavs kept their heads to run out comfortable winners.
Two of Obradovic's key players are doubtful for Sunday's game.
Aleksandar Djordjevic did not start the match and was troubled by a leg injury throughout the game, particularly in the final time-out.
The injury may limit Djordjevic's role in the final, while fellow guard Predrag Danilovic pulled up at the end of the semifinal with an ankle injury.
All four semifinalists have already guaranteed places in next year's world championships.
